title: Watch Configurator with Strap Swap
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a Three.js-based watch configurator that loads a 3D model and allows users to configure a watch with different strap options. Follow these specifications exactly:

## Scene Setup
1. Create a Three.js scene with a dark gradient background (top: #1a1a2e, bottom: #16213e).
2. Add a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at the origin.
3. Add OrbitControls with damping enabled, limited polar angle (0.3 to 1.4 radians), and min/max distance (3, 8).
4. Add three lights: an AmbientLight (0xffffff, 0.4), a DirectionalLight (0xffffff, 0.8) at (5, 10, 5), and a PointLight (0xffd700, 0.5) at (-3, 3, -3).
5. Load the model 'ABeautifulGame.glb' using GLTFLoader. Center and scale the model so it fits within a 2-unit bounding sphere. Position it at the origin. This model represents the watch body/display piece.

## Watch Strap System
Create a procedural watch strap using Three.js geometry (two elongated rounded box shapes or extruded shapes) positioned above and below the loaded model to simulate top and bottom straps. Each strap segment should be a separate mesh.

## Strap Materials (5 options)
Define 5 strap configurations:
- 'leather_brown': { color: 0x8B4513, roughness: 0.8, metalness: 0.1, name: 'Brown Leather' }
- 'leather_black': { color: 0x1a1a1a, roughness: 0.7, metalness: 0.1, name: 'Black Leather' }
- 'metal_silver': { color: 0xC0C0C0, roughness: 0.3, metalness: 0.9, name: 'Silver Metal' }
- 'metal_gold': { color: 0xFFD700, roughness: 0.3, metalness: 0.9, name: 'Gold Metal' }
- 'rubber_sport': { color: 0x2d3436, roughness: 0.9, metalness: 0.0, name: 'Sport Rubber' }

## UI Elements
1. Create a title bar at the top: 'WATCH CONFIGURATOR' in white, font-size 24px, centered.
2. Create a strap selector panel on the left side with 5 circular color swatch buttons (40px diameter each), each with a 2px border. The active swatch should have a gold (#FFD700) border. Each button should have id='swatch_{strap_key}' (e.g., 'swatch_leather_brown').
3. Display the current strap name below the swatches in a div with id='strap_label'.
4. Add a 'Rotate' toggle button (id='btn_rotate') that enables/disables auto-rotation of the model (0.5 deg/frame around Y axis).
5. Add a 'Zoom Fit' button (id='btn_zoom_fit') that animates the camera to the default position (0, 2, 5) over 30 frames.
6. Add a price display (id='price_display') showing prices: leather_brown=$149, leather_black=$159, metal_silver=$299, metal_gold=$499, rubber_sport=$89.
7. Add a 'Screenshot Mode' button (id='btn_screenshot') that hides all UI and changes background to white, and toggles back on second click.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- modelLoaded: boolean, true once GLB is loaded
- currentStrap: string, the strap key (default 'leather_brown')
- strapColor: hex number of current strap material color
- strapMetalness: number, metalness of current strap
- strapRoughness: number, roughness of current strap
- autoRotate: boolean (default false)
- modelRotationY: number, current Y rotation in radians
- cameraDistance: number, distance from camera to origin
- price: number, current price
- screenshotMode: boolean (default false)
- strapChangeCount: number, how many times strap has been changed (starts 0)
- zoomFitActive: boolean, true while zoom animation is running

## Interactions
- Clicking a swatch button changes both strap meshes to that material, updates currentStrap, strapColor, strapMetalness, strapRoughness, price, increments strapChangeCount, and updates the strap_label text and active swatch border.
- The Rotate button toggles autoRotate. When active, the model (and straps) rotate around Y axis.
- Zoom Fit smoothly moves camera back to default position.
- Screenshot Mode toggles UI visibility and background color.

## Animation
Use requestAnimationFrame loop. When autoRotate is true, increment model's Y rotation by 0.00873 radians per frame (~0.5 degrees). Always update __3D_STATE__ each frame.

Start with leather_brown strap selected, autoRotate off, screenshotMode off.
physics_constraints: Camera distance must remain between 3 and 8 units. Model rotation should be continuous and NaN-free. Strap material properties must exactly match the defined configurations.
